ticket.title: Emit one span per CLI invocation across the suite
ticket.description: One of twelve tools emits spans and only for provider completions, so the panel observes inference and nothing else, while telemetry is meant to be suite-wide: observability plus the metadata half of the training corpus. Shape: one span per CLI invocation from a shared helper in gaugeblock-workspace called at each main boundary (binary, command, repo, branch, task_key when a claim is held, duration, status, first diagnostic), plus nested spans for sub-operations joined by trace_id and parent_span_id, which sawhorse already mints correctly. Payloads stay out by design: no prompt or completion text, and the join to the spool is span.task_key, so training data comes from spool records joined to spans rather than from the spans themselves. Retention becomes configurable (max_bytes, keep_rotations, retain) with raw logs untracked and rotated; tracked retained aggregates are a deliberate exception and stay disabled until more than one tool emits.
acceptance_criteria: nine more tools emit; a task cost is answerable from spans alone; no span carries payload text; rotation leaves the raw log untracked and the aggregate tracked

MECHANISM DONE 2026-11-08 (commit cb516f3), WIRING OWED. No caller yet.

InvocationSpan::start(binary, command) opens a span at a process boundary, records command, repository (suite member
name, else checkout directory) and branch, and closes with Ok or Error; dropping without finishing records it as
running. sink_path moved beside it, since where an invocation writes is that module's subject, and telemetry.rs had
reached 258 lines.

WHY NO CALLER IN THIS COMMIT: wiring needs gaugeblock-workspace added to CLI crates that do not have it - batten has
none anywhere, chalkline/rabbet/sawhorse have it only in their cores. That is a dependency decision per crate. I tried
chalkline first, hit the missing dependency, and reverted rather than smuggling it in at the end of a session. The
measurement is recorded here so the next attempt starts from it instead of discovering it again.

NEXT STEPS, in order:
  1. wire ONE tool end to end and prove the span appears in the suite log with binary, command, repo and duration;
  2. add the dependency to the remaining CLI crates, one commit each;
  3. only then is the epic's coverage claim meaningful - nine tools emitting is the point, not the helper existing.

A mechanism with no caller is exactly the failure this session catalogued five times (a reader never called, a
chain never run, a table column never written). It is recorded as owed rather than described as delivered.
